tagline: A Mediterranean island where the coast road is slow and the sea is fast — Limassol, Larnaca, Paphos and Ayia Napa on one calm shore.
summary: Cyprus is an eastern-Mediterranean island whose population and tourism cluster along the southern coast — the marinas and business district of Limassol, the airport city of Larnaca, the resort coast of Ayia Napa and Protaras, and Paphos to the west. The coast road links them slowly; the calm Mediterranean sea links them directly. With major marinas (Limassol Marina, Ayia Napa Marina), a large resort economy and warm, sheltered water, Cyprus is a clean fit for a coastal foiling tier between its main coastal cities.
why_marine_mobility: Cyprus's southern cities string along one calm coast, slow by road but fast by sea. Navier's Pioneer II flies the coastal corridors — Limassol to Larnaca, Larnaca to Ayia Napa and Protaras, the airport transfers — on warm, sheltered Mediterranean water off the island's modern marinas, while the Quanta-LR range would open longer connections toward the Greek islands and the Levant coast. It is a resort-and-business market where the water is a genuine time-saver.

demand_signals.label: Limassol & Ayia Napa marinas
demand_signals.note: Limassol Marina and Ayia Napa Marina anchor a high-spend yachting, business and resort economy along the southern coast.

demand_signals.label: Coastal-city corridor
demand_signals.note: Limassol, Larnaca, Paphos and the Ayia Napa resort coast are linked only by a congested coast road and motorway — direct sea routes are far shorter.

demand_signals.label: Airport-to-resort transfers
demand_signals.note: Larnaca and Paphos airports feed a large tourism market scattered along the coast, with slow road transfers to the eastern resorts.

use_cases.body: A coastal foiling tier linking Limassol's business and marina district to Larnaca and the airport, and on to the Ayia Napa and Protaras resort coast, cutting slow road transfers.
Premium marina-to-marina hops between Limassol Marina, Larnaca Marina and Ayia Napa Marina for the yachting and business market.
Fast airport-to-resort sea transfers from Larnaca to the eastern beaches on calm Mediterranean water.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The southern-coast mesh — Larnaca↔Ayia Napa (~19 nm), Larnaca↔Protaras (~23 nm), Limassol↔Larnaca (~35 nm), Larnaca Airport↔Limassol (~35 nm) — sits inside the 70 nm all-electric range on warm, sheltered Mediterranean water off modern marinas.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The longer legs — Limassol↔Paphos (~40 nm) and Limassol↔Ayia Napa (~52 nm) sit near the upper all-electric envelope, while Quanta-LR hybrid range would open connections toward the Greek Dodecanese and the Levant coast without charging dependency.

signature_routes.label: Limassol Marina ↔ Larnaca Marina (all-electric coastal corridor)

transit_planning: For the Cyprus Ports Authority, the Deputy Ministry of Tourism or a marina operator: a clean coastal tier linking the southern cities and airports, integrated with the island's marina infrastructure and large resort economy.
competitive_landscape: Cyprus has no scheduled coastal passenger water transport between its cities — movement is by congested coast road and motorway, with the sea used for charters and leisure. The modern marinas provide ready anchors for a greenfield foiling tier with no incumbent ferry to displace.
regulatory_note: Maritime activity falls under the Cyprus Deputy Ministry of Shipping and the Cyprus Ports Authority, within the EU framework. The island's tourism-and-marina investment agenda and warm, sheltered southern coast provide a supportive environment for a clean coastal water-transport tier.
seasonality: A long, warm Mediterranean season (April–November) drives resort and leisure demand, with the southern coast calm and sheltered for most of the year; peak summer heat favours air-conditioned electric cabins, and winter activity is thinner but the coast remains largely navigable.
